system:
You are diagnosing why one merchant's payment
success rate is below what their category achieves. Before answering, you
may look things up.

Ask for ONE lookup at a time. You will be shown the result, then may ask
again. The budget is small, so ask for what would actually change your
mind rather than for what confirms what you already believe.

Stop as soon as you have enough. Stopping early is a good outcome.

Reply with JSON and nothing else, one of:
  {"tool": "name", "args": {...}, "why": "what this would tell you"}
  {"done": true, "why": "what you now believe and what convinced you"}
prompt:
CONTEXT
MERCHANT
  name: VoltBill Utilities
  mcc: 4900 (utilities)
  transactions this month: 2100
  average ticket: Rs 2421.52

SUCCESS RATE
  observed:            85.90%
  cohort achievable:   89.95%
  gap:                 4.04 points

DECOMPOSITION (Shapley, points of the gap)
  bank          +0.01 pts +/- 0.57 measured error   [INSIDE ITS OWN ERROR BAR]
  method        +0.02 pts +/- 0.57 measured error   [INSIDE ITS OWN ERROR BAR]
  hour          +4.26 pts +/- 0.57 measured error   [NOT IDENTIFIED - merchant has effectively one value here]
  amount_band   -0.04 pts +/- 0.58 measured error   [INSIDE ITS OWN ERROR BAR]
  residual      -0.21 pts   [unexplained residual]
  process_gap   +2.61 pts   [process gap, computed directly, NOT decomposed]

MERCHANT BANK MIX vs NPCI NATIONAL DATA (period 2025-08)
  bank                              share   NPCI BD%%  NPCI TD%%  approved%%
  State Bank of India               27.8%     5.92     0.42     93.66
  HDFC Bank Ltd.                     9.0%     4.63     0.01     95.37
  Bank of Baroda                     7.0%     8.50     0.05     91.44
  Punjab National Bank               6.2%     8.61     0.19     91.20
  Union Bank of India                6.0%     7.02     0.75     92.23
  Canara Bank                        5.4%     6.92     0.36     92.73

HOUR DISTRIBUTION (share of payments)

TOOLS
  factor_breakdown(factor) -- Volume share and failure rate for every value of a factor. factor: bank | method | hour | amount_band
  bank_vs_npci(bank) -- This merchant's failure rate on one issuer against NPCI's published national figures for it. bank: exact bank name
  failure_examples(factor, value) -- Real failed payments matching a factor value, with their error codes. factor: bank|method|hour|amount_band, value: the value
  attribution_with_error(factor) -- What the decomposition attributes to a factor, beside its own measured error. factor: bank | method | hour | amount_band

ASKED SO FAR
  factor_breakdown({"factor":"hour"}) -> {"factor":"hour","breakdown":[]}
  factor_breakdown({"factor":"method"}) -> {"factor":"method","breakdown":[]}
  factor_breakdown({"factor":"amount_band"}) -> {"factor":"amount_band","breakdown":[]}
text: {"tool": "factor_breakdown", "args": {"factor": "bank"}, "why": "The hour factor has the largest Shapley contribution (+4.26 pts) but is flagged as 'effectively one value' so it can't be acted on. The process_gap (+2.61 pts) is the next largest actionable signal. Before going there, I want to see if any specific bank is driving failures beyond what NPCI benchmarks would predict — that would be the most actionable finding."}
